image_description: A large sturgeon swimming in an aquarium tank, viewed through glass. The fish has a dark gray/brown dorsal side and lighter ventral side. Visible features include the elongated body, dorsal fin, pectoral fins, pelvic fins, anal fin, and heterocercal tail. Bony scutes are visible along the lateral line and dorsal ridge. The head is partially visible but the snout tip and mouth area are somewhat obscured by angle and water refraction. Barbels are not clearly distinguishable due to image resolution and viewing angle.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Elongated head with protrusible mouth on ventral surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head is visible but the ventral mouth structure is obscured by the viewing angle (side profile from above) and water refraction. Cannot confirm protrusible nature or exact ventral position.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Four barbels (sensory whiskers) anterior to mouth.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Barbels are small structures located on the underside of the snout. From this elevated side-angle view through aquarium glass, they are not resolvable. Marked untestable rather than absent to avoid false negative.
The snout is clearly visible and exhibits the characteristic pointed, conical shape typical of sturgeons.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Elongated fusiform body with impressively large, extended proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The body is distinctly elongated and fusiform, occupying a significant portion of the frame, consistent with sturgeon morphology.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Five rows of bony scutes (plates) along body instead of scales.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Distinct rows of bony scutes are visible along the dorsal midline and lateral line. While all five rows aren't simultaneously visible due to angle, the presence of characteristic scutes instead of scales is confirmed.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Gray, brown, or black dorsally with lighter ventral surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The fish displays clear countershading: dark gray/brown on the dorsal side transitioning to a lighter, pale ventral surface.

The caudal fin is clearly visible and exhibits the classic heterocercal structure where the upper lobe is larger and extends further than the lower lobe, with the vertebral column extending into the upper lobe.
